title: Nuclear-powered airplane in an Idaho Falls hangar

tellings.quote: >> Jesse, this goes back decades. If I told you there is an airplane powered by nuclear power sitting in a hanger in Idaho Falls, would you believe me?
there is an airplane powered by nuclear power sitting in a hanger in Idaho Falls. Would you believe me?
tellings.difference: Credits Howard Hughes, and leaves out 'this goes back decades'.
tellings.link_reason: The same remark by the same official about a nuclear-powered airplane sitting in a hangar in Idaho Falls.

plain: An airplane powered by a nuclear reactor is sitting in a hangar in Idaho Falls, Idaho. John S. Herrington, introduced on the show as a former Secretary of Energy, puts this to Michels as a question: "If I told you there is an airplane powered by nuclear power sitting in a hanger in Idaho Falls, would you believe me?" He says "this goes back decades," and at another point he credits Howard Hughes with it. He raises it as an example of old, advanced technology the public never hears about.
